This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing regression bisection code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing regression bisection style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about regression bisection explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Before starting regression bisection work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
3. Prefer the simplest regression bisection approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
4. Prefer explicit, readable regression bisection solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. Re-check edge cases relevant to regression bisection (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
6. Measure before optimizing any regression bisection bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. When regression bisection decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Validate regression bisection outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
9. Document any non-obvious regression bisection decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
10. Surface known limitations of a chosen regression bisection approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not skip documenting regression bisection assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new regression bisection abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated regression bisection concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of regression bisection correctness.
- Do not silently drop regression bisection edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about regression bisection over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
